what_it_does: Electronic noses are arrays of chemical sensors that detect gases for industrial safety, food quality, and environmental monitoring. Existing designs use small arrays with generic sensors, and they get tired: once a molecule sticks to a sensor surface, it lingers, poisoning future measurements. This paper integrates 4,096 molecular-selective sensors on a single chip using metal-organic frameworks (MOFs)—crystalline materials designed to capture specific molecules. Each sensor sits right next to a heating element that can thermodynamically kick absorbed molecules off the surface, enabling rapid sensor regeneration. The on-chip heat control and readout electronics create a complete real-time gas-detection system suitable for dense deployment.
